subject: pathology
title: Membranoproliferative Pattern, Tram-Track Glomerulus, Complement, and C3 Glomerulopathy

steps.tx: Membranoproliferative pattern duplicates basement membrane around interposed mesangial deposits, double contours shining as tram tracks on silver stain while lobulation and hypercellularity crowd tufts. That duplication is the **tram-track (double contour) glomerulus of MPGN pattern**. Silver stain makes the duplicated membrane black and crisp, which is why pathologists reach for it first here.
steps.say: Tram tracks mean new basement membrane wrapped around deposits and cells; find why complement or complexes built them.

vis.caption: Membranoproliferative pattern with lobulation and double contour basement membranes.

steps.tx: Modern classification asks mechanism before morphology: immune complex disease from infections, lupus, and monoclonal proteins versus complement dysregulation of C3 glomerulopathy by immunofluorescence dominance. That reorganisation is **MPGN reclassification, immune complex versus C3 glomerulopathy**. C3 dominance means C3 staining at least two orders of intensity stronger than any immunoglobulin on immunofluorescence.
steps.say: Do not sign MPGN pattern without asking complexes or complement; immunofluorescence dominance decides the road.

steps.tx: Dense deposit disease, C3 glomerulopathy's electron dense ribbon within basement membrane, strikes young patients with low C3, drusen eye deposits, and lipodystrophy associations. The ribbon lesion is **dense deposit disease of C3 glomerulopathy**. C3 nephritic factor, an autoantibody stabilising the alternative pathway convertase, is found in most dense deposit cases.
steps.say: Ribbon dense membrane, low C3, young patient: dense deposit disease within C3 glomerulopathy.

steps.tx: Low C4 with low C3 suggests classical pathway immune complexes, isolated low C3 suggests alternative pathway complement disease, cryoglobulins consuming C4 dramatically. That complement compass is **C3 and C4 patterns in glomerulonephritis**. Hepatitis C with cryoglobulinaemia is the classic infection behind an immune complex MPGN picture in adults.
steps.say: C4 falls with classical complexes, C3 alone falls with alternative complement disease; let complement navigate.

steps.tx: Monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance hides small clones injuring kidney through proliferative glomerulonephritis with monoclonal deposits, demanding clone hunting by electrophoresis, free light chains, and marrow. That small clone danger is **monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance (MGRS)**. The term exists precisely because the clone may be too small to meet myeloma criteria yet still destroys kidneys.
steps.say: A tiny clone can wreck a kidney; proliferative deposits earn full paraprotein hunting regardless of spike size.

vis.alt: Monoclonal plasma cell clone with paraprotein
vis.caption: A monoclonal plasma cell clone producing paraprotein, the small clone that must be hunted in monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance.

steps.tx: Transplant recurrence stalks C3 glomerulopathy and monoclonal deposit diseases, counselling recipients and sometimes selecting prophylactic complement strategies in trials. That recurrence honesty is **glomerular disease recurrence after transplantation**. Dense deposit disease recurs in the great majority of grafts, often within the first two years after transplant.
steps.say: Counsel recurrence plainly in C3 and monoclonal diseases; grafts inherit the original battlefield.

steps.tx: Supportive RAAS blockade, blood pressure, sodium, and lipid control underpin every MPGN mechanism therapy, because proteinuria itself accelerates scarring regardless of deposits. That foundation is **antiproteinuric support across glomerular diseases**. Dietary sodium under 2 grams daily noticeably strengthens the antiproteinuric effect of RAAS blockade.
steps.say: Whatever built the deposits, block RAAS and pressure; proteinuria scars kidneys on its own schedule.

steps.tx: Eculizumab and emerging complement inhibitors serve selected C3 glomerulopathy and thrombotic microangiopathy patients by genetics, biopsy activity, and trial access rather than pattern alone. Selection discipline defines **complement inhibitor selection in glomerular disease**. Eculizumab blocks C5, so meningococcal vaccination must precede it because terminal complement defence is switched off.
steps.say: Complement drugs follow mechanism proof, not pattern panic; genetics and activity select their patients.
